jane.cust: Hey team — production started returning 401 invalid_api_key around ~22:15 UTC after we ran our org SSO key rotation. No code changes. Example curl below, response body is 401 with invalid_api_key. Any quick checks?

sami.support: sorry to hear that. Can you paste the exact 401 response headers (especially x-request-id and x-redwood-org) and the curl you used? Also which key did you rotate — user or service account?

jane.cust: here's the curl we run from our backend (node):

```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY'
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json'
  -d '{"model":"rw-model-1","prompt":"hello"}'
```

401 response headers we get: x-request-id: rq_0d3a9f, x-redwood-org: acme-inc, date: Tue, 16 Mar 2026 22:15:02 GMT
response body: { error: "invalid_api_key", message: "API key expired or revoked" }
we rotated keys via SSO provisioner earlier today, we rotated the service account key.

lucy.ops: quick note — after org-wide SSO rotations we also revoke linked service keys for safety. Did you create a replacement key in the console or via the provisioning API?

jane.cust: yes, new key was created by the SSO flow and we updated the env var on one app instance, but not all pods restarted yet. We assumed the old key would keep working for a short TTL but looks like it was immediately revoked.

sami.support: Two likely causes here: 1) the rotated key was immediately revoked (no grace window) and your remaining instances are still using the old key; or 2) the new key is scoped or org-bound differently. Can you run this from one of the failing pods to confirm which key is being sent (redact the key):

```
curl -i -X GET https://httpbin.org/headers -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" -H "x-redwood-org: acme-inc"
```

kevin.sre: Also check that the x-redwood-org header matches your org slug. If a key is org-bound and you send the wrong header or omit it, API will return invalid_api_key even if key is valid.

jane.cust: ran the header check on failing pod, it showed Authorization: Bearer <OLD_KEY_REDACTED> and x-redwood-org: acme-inc — so pod definitely using the old key.

sami.support: ok that confirms immediate revocation. Steps to remediate: 1) rotate env var across all instances and rollout; 2) if you need a short-term workaround, create a temporary service key in the console with the same scopes and org binding and deploy it; 3) if the rotation was accidental, we can re-activate the revoked key from the admin panel but only for a short window — ping us if you want us to re-activate while you patch.

jane.cust: we'll rollout the new key now. one question — why did one instance pick up the new key earlier? we updated env var via config map and one pod restarted, others are on older image so didn't reload.

lucy.ops: configmap update triggers pod restart only if you roll the deployment or use a reload controller. Manual pod restarts will pick it up. In k8s we recommend a rolling restart: kubectl rollout restart deploy/my-backend.

kevin.sre: additional recommendation: enable the short-lived provisioning flow with auto-rotate hooks (our docs show how to wire the SSO provider to the provisioning API) so keys are automatically refreshed across pods. Also add a small healthcheck that fails on 401 and triggers a restart, so you avoid stale key drift.

sami.support: closing loop with a small checklist for you to confirm: - all pods restarted and showing new key in header check - no 401s in logs after rollout - if you need us to re-activate old key, reply and we'll do a 10-min reactivation window while you patch all instances.

jane.cust: rolled out new key cluster-wide, ran header check on 5 pods — all show new key. 401s stopped. Thanks! :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: deployment my-backend restarted by jane.cust (rolling restart) — 5/5 pods ready

sami.support: great, marking this thread resolved. If you want, we can schedule a quick runbook review for SSO rotation behavior so your rotation process includes a staged rollout.

jane.cust: would appreciate that. please open a short runbook doc and assign to lucy.ops.

sami.support: will do, assigning follow-up. Thanks!
